prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Edit target: the attached existing game sprite sheet. This is an art replacement for a live game, not a new concept layout.
Primary request: make this same main character look a bit more like Henry of Skalitz from Kingdom Come: Deliverance, translated into this exact medieval woodcut style.

Change the FACE AND HAIR in the eight bareheaded figures in the TOP TWO ROWS consistently: a young adult working-class man, short practical medium-brown cropped hair with a slightly irregular fringe, fuller broader cheeks, solid square jaw, a short natural straight nose, normal-size ears, faint stubble, a mildly stubborn and slightly bewildered expression. Henry-like approachable sturdy peasant rather than the current old gaunt sharp-nosed sneering man. No quiff or spiky swept-back hair. No exaggerated nose. Small eyes obscured by the same narrow brow shadows; do not give him large bright cartoon eyes. Slightly fill out the neck to fit the younger face, without changing any joints, silhouette proportions or shoulder placement. Same identity in all eight frames.

LOCK EVERYTHING ELSE: preserve the existing 1448 x 1086 canvas, four columns by three rows, 362 x 362 cells. Keep all bodies, walking poses, hands, foot positions, frame placement, scales, boots, patched dirty cloth tunics, belts, folds, swords, and orange accents exactly as supplied. Preserve the third/bottom helmeted row unchanged, including the CLOSED cylindrical helmet. All eight updated heads point right at the same existing profile angle and stay at their existing positions. Match their pose-specific head tilts. Do not redraw or rearrange the gait.

Style invariants: worn irregular BLACK medieval woodcut outlines and carved crosshatching, flat warm off-white opaque material interiors, tiny dirty pale orange accents. Match the existing sprite sheet's ink thickness and hatching density. Scruffy absurd medieval comedy. No soft painted shading, glow, gloss, photorealism, Disney face or chibi proportions. No labels, text, grid, ground, contact shadows or background.
Output: truly transparent RGBA outside each character, fully opaque character interiors and clean contours without grey or coloured halos.
postprocessing: Previously authorised alpha cleanup: threshold 180, opaque interiors. Original helmeted row is retained via its original atlas reference.
